summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA 2008)** — kinship-care incentives  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — reimbursement for approved kin placements

primary_citations.citation_text: Montana - Title 41, Chapter 3 (Child Abuse and Neglect – mandatory reporting and protective services)

regulations_applicable.title: Department 37 - PUBLIC HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Termination of an incarcerated father's rights to an Indian child was affirmed and the placement ruling left undisturbed: the caseworker's testimony that she visited him in jail, arranged visitation and made referrals satisfied ICWA's active-efforts requirement even though the ICWA expert did not testify on that subject.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Montana case on how the § 1915 placement preferences are litigated, and on what active efforts look like when the parent is incarcerated.
key_cases.quote: The statutory requirement is that the State “shall satisfy the court that active efforts have been made.”

key_cases.holding: Reversed: once the father completed his court-ordered treatment plan, the district court unconstitutionally violated his fundamental right to parent by permanently placing the child with the maternal grandmother, a nonparent, and denying him placement; the abuse and neglect proceeding should have been dismissed at that point.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that a kinship placement cannot be made permanent over a fit parent who has completed his treatment plan.
key_cases.quote: At that time, this proceeding should have been dismissed, leaving further consideration of the parenting relationship and parenting plan establishment in the DR matter.

key_cases.holding: Termination of an out-of-state, non-custodial father's rights was reversed for ineffective assistance of counsel and the case rewound to the adjudication stage: on removal from the custodial parent the Department must first consider placement with the non-custodial parent after a preliminary assessment, and may expand the investigation or impose an ICPC or treatment plan only where objective, demonstrable circumstances show an imminent safety risk.
key_cases.relevance: It requires the Department to look to the non-custodial parent before a foster or kinship placement, and holds that a completed ICPC or treatment plan is not a precondition to that placement at the outset.
key_cases.quote: Upon removal of a child from a custodial parent, the Department must first consider placement of the child with the non-custodial parent.

statutory_basis.citation_text: Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-427(1)(d), (2) — the court grants an order for immediate protection and emergency protective services, including temporary medical or out-of-home care, on probable cause, or on clear and convincing evidence if the case is subject to the federal Indian Child Welfare Act or the Montana Indian Child Welfare Act; same standard as § 41-3-422(5)(a)(i)

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: No judicial probable-cause finding authorizing removal to continue beyond 5 business days; if the court finds continued removal is not appropriate the child must be returned immediately (Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-306(1)(a), (6)). No hearing is required if the child is released prior to the time of the required hearing (§ 41-3-306(1)(c))

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to know where child is going
what_to_say: Do you have a court order for removal?
What is the specific imminent danger?
Where are you taking my child?
